medicalHistory.lastOralIntake: Not clinically significant for dental emergency

incidentDescription: Bike accident with direct impact to upper anterior teeth. Patient reported fractured maxillary right central incisor, upper lip swelling, cold sensitivity, and pain while biting. No loss of consciousness, nausea, vomiting, facial bone fracture, TMJ abnormality, tooth displacement, or root fracture.
complaints: Broken upper front tooth after bike accident
Sensitivity to cold water and air

structuredComplaints.complaint: Fractured maxillary right central incisor after road traffic accident
structuredComplaints.provocation: Biting, mastication, cold water, and air exposure
structuredComplaints.timing: Persistent since trauma with stimulus-related exacerbation
structuredComplaints.associatedSymptoms: Bleeding from upper lip and gums immediately after trauma, upper labial mucosal laceration, mild gingival inflammation around tooth 11

diagnosis: Ellis Class III complicated crown fracture of maxillary right central incisor (tooth 11) with pulp exposure, associated subluxation injury, and upper labial soft tissue laceration. No root fracture, alveolar fracture, tooth displacement, or periapical pathology identified.
treatmentProvided: Emergency dental trauma management was completed under local anesthesia and rubber dam isolation. Endodontic access was gained through the fracture site, coronal pulp was removed, working length was determined using apex locator and radiographic confirmation, canals were cleaned and shaped with crown-down instrumentation, irrigated with 3% sodium hypochlorite, saline, and 17% EDTA, obturated with gutta-percha and AH Plus sealer, restored with fiber post, dual-cure resin cement, composite core build-up, and provisional crown.
treatmentPlan: Definitive rehabilitation with lithium disilicate (E-max) full ceramic crown after 7-day review. Verify shade, marginal fit, proximal contacts, and occlusion before resin cementation. Follow-up at 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, and annually. Monitor pain, mobility, percussion response, pulp/endodontic status, discoloration, gingival healing, periodontal ligament space, periapical changes, root resorption, crown margins, restoration integrity, and occlusion.
dietAdvice: Soft diet for the initial post-treatment period.
Avoid biting hard foods directly with tooth 11 until definitive crown cementation.
Maintain oral hygiene with gentle brushing around the injured area.
Report swelling, spontaneous pain, fever, sinus tract, crown loosening, or recurrent trauma immediately.
notes: Title: Management of a complicated crown fracture of maxillary right central incisor following trauma - clinical case report.
Patient preserved the fractured tooth fragment in milk and brought it to the clinic.
Extraoral findings: mild upper lip swelling, healing abrasion on lower chin, no facial asymmetry, no mandibular deviation, TMJ movements normal.
Intraoral soft tissue findings: healing upper labial mucosal laceration and mild gingival inflammation around tooth 11.
Hard tissue findings: oblique crown fracture involving mesio-incisal angle of tooth 11, extending from incisal edge toward cervical third, with visible pulp exposure and bleeding from pulp chamber.
Clinical tests: cold test positive, heat test positive, EPT delayed response, percussion tender, palpation negative, Grade I mobility.
Prognosis: good with preserved tooth structure, no root fracture, immediate treatment, and maintained follow-up.
One-year outcome target: asymptomatic tooth, stable crown, healthy gingiva, intact periapical structures, no root resorption, satisfactory esthetic and functional outcome.
primaryImpression: Complicated crown fracture of tooth 11 due to road traffic accident
secondaryImpression: Subluxation injury and upper labial mucosal laceration
medicationsAdministered: 2% lignocaine with 1:80,000 adrenaline for local anesthesia
proceduresPerformed: Clinical and radiographic dental trauma assessment
Working length determination with apex locator and radiograph
Biomechanical preparation using crown-down technique with ProTaper Gold files
Irrigation with 3% sodium hypochlorite, saline, and 17% EDTA
Obturation with gutta-percha and AH Plus sealer
Fiber post placement with 4 mm apical gutta-percha seal maintained
Lithium disilicate E-max crown try-in and resin cementation

structuredMedications.indication: Pain control for endodontic and restorative treatment

structuredProcedures.notes: Working length 23 mm; obturation confirmed radiographically.

structuredProcedures.procedureName: Fiber post and composite core build-up
structuredProcedures.notes: Post space prepared after gutta-percha removal while preserving 4 mm apical seal; fiber post cemented with dual-cure resin cement.
Bis-acryl provisional crown cemented temporarily after full ceramic crown preparation.
E-max crown try-in, shade verification, occlusal check, and resin cementation completed.

clinicalData.discussion: Traumatic anterior tooth fractures are common in young adults after falls, sports injuries, and road traffic accidents. Maxillary central incisors are commonly involved due to their anterior position. In a mature permanent tooth with complicated crown fracture and pulp exposure, root canal treatment followed by fiber post-supported ceramic restoration can restore function and esthetics with favorable prognosis when follow-up is maintained.
clinicalData.conclusion: The patient presented with Ellis Class III fracture of tooth 11 following road traffic accident. Endodontic therapy, fiber post placement, composite core build-up, and E-max crown rehabilitation restored esthetics and function with favorable follow-up findings.
